doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Reading a poetic review of Habitat
summary: Rowe reads a lyrical web review of Habitat; Jensen says she does not think of her music in such terms but values people's engagement.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: I want to read an excerpt and I’m wondering if you’ve heard this. It’s from a website called Jazz DiGamma, which I believe came from a fellow in Brooklyn. And it’s really, really lengthy, I’m going to read a small part of it if I can. It’s referring to “Habitat.” Christine Jensen’s “Habitat.” And it says, “Its lines leap off planes to join other lines that leap off other planes, there to reconstitute in harmonic progressions that entwine like the double helix of a musical DNA that is subtle and nimble and barely discernable but in actual fact it is arthoscopically formed by other lines that shape this gorgeous musical icosehedron.
Wow. Can you send that to me?

Wow. And it goes on and on. This fellow is like a poet and I will send you the link to it. But I think I had a question there, and that is, it’s two parts. What do you think about when you hear something like that? And do you think of your own music in such deep and poetic terms?

I do not. I wish I could. I think that’s a reflection off of my art through their art in a way, with the art of word and I wish I could do that but I think my artwork ended up in music. And I mean I think it’s the greatest gift back to me is when people really are engaged in anything I do. I’m not making them do it. You know what I mean? I’m not like you have to sit down and listen to me. I’m more like here’s my attempt at describing my feelings and my thoughts and my process and I’m putting it out and hopefully I get something back through things like that actually, whether they do a painting or they’re on a drive and they hear the music and they’re like you made the environment look different or something.
